bug_semantics: ScriptRange multiplication repeated a lazy left-hand sequence in an attacker-controlled outer for-loop but charged TemplateContext.StepLoop only inside the inner foreach. When the lazy sequence yielded no elements, the inner loop and StepLoop call never ran, so a tiny template could force up to int.MaxValue uncharged repetitions despite LoopLimit, consuming a CPU core and creating garbage-collection pressure.
flaw_origin: Commit 7d73abb515f942dd71f8797506356bbe6383b3be introduced ScriptRange and its array-multiplication dispatch. In src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs, the new MultiplyImpl at lines 175-181 looped count times and enumerated left inside that loop without independently bounding or charging each repetition; TryEvaluate at line 359 routed ScriptRange multiplication directly to that implementation. Later commit dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9 added an item-level StepLoop call but retained the already-vulnerable outer-loop structure, so it was not the first origin.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p on the BIC commit object shows author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, and only the message 'Add better support for ranges via ScriptRange. Add IScriptTransformable.'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-89cf-6hmv-8rxm identifies src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs, the empty-lazy-sequence LoopLimit bypass, affected NuGet versions >=3.0.0 and <=7.2.5, and patched version 7.2.6; the public alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-25v3-x2wq-mm38. git log -L 367,381:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs at vulnerable head c3f03bfc912e14b306a01a03e611f606b05f9c33 traced the current helper through dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9 to the original ScriptRange file, and git log -S 'for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)' independently found 7d73abb515f942dd71f8797506356bbe6383b3be as the first commit of that loop. The BIC source is https://github.com/scriban/scriban/blob/7d73abb515f942dd71f8797506356bbe6383b3be/src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs#L170-L181 and its operator dispatch is at #L359. Direct-parent verification with git cat-file -e '8aa9acc7df5e7783fd51b1ffbdacf80a29f4edf3:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptRange.cs' failed because the path does not exist in that tree; the BIC diff is a new file from /dev/null, proving the vulnerable implementation absent in the immediate parent. git tag --contains showed the BIC in 3.0.0, 7.2.5, and 7.2.6; the peeled release commits are 3.0.0=9014ab459103c212f7777c57e8c6c62a890fc032, 7.2.5=8872919995b8baae3008c2d3be6f0fad04e812ac, and 7.2.6=420513a9d017fa54b23ba78a9f21a12187a8dd97. At tag 7.2.5, ScriptRange.cs lines 368-380 still place StepLoop only inside foreach. Direct fix https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/973edd1f1c10fae7d3a8650ac0d309d52072102c adds a repetition StepLoop before foreach and separate item accounting, plus regression cases LazyArrayMultiplyShouldRespectLoopLimitForEmptySequence and LazyArrayMultiplyShouldAllowWorkWithinLoopLimit in src/Scriban.Tests/TestRuntime.cs. git tag --contains showed this fix only in 7.2.6 among the three boundary tags, not 3.0.0 or 7.2.5; tag 7.2.6's ScriptRange.cs lines 368-380 retains the essential fix by calling StepLoop at line 374 before entering foreach.
reasoning: The advisory's attack is possible because multiplication performs work once per requested repetition even when the lazy input emits zero items, while the vulnerable code accounted only for emitted items. The earliest public-history implementation of that exact nested-loop mechanism is the one-parent, non-squash commit 7d73abb515f942dd71f8797506356bbe6383b3be: it created ScriptRange.cs, added MultiplyImpl's count-controlled outer loop, and wired the multiply operator to it. The file's absence from direct parent 8aa9acc7df5e7783fd51b1ffbdacf80a29f4edf3 proves parent absence; the later 2026 LoopLimit change merely preserved the pre-existing unbounded outer repetition while adding incomplete inner accounting, so choosing it would misidentify a later partial hardening as the origin. The BIC is contained in the first affected stable tag 3.0.0. Commit 973edd1f1c10fae7d3a8650ac0d309d52072102c directly closes the bypass by charging every outer repetition even for an empty sequence, is absent from 7.2.5, and is contained in patched tag 7.2.6. AI attribution is therefore judged solely from the proven BIC commit object, whose human author/committer and trailer-free message contain no AI marker; later commit markers are irrelevant to the BIC-only rule.
